**Alert fatigue** is one of the most underappreciated failure modes in health AI.

An AI can be technically accurate and still make things *worse* — if it fires too many alerts, clinicians start ignoring them. The tool trains the humans around it to tune it out.

[EX]Epic's sepsis prediction model — deployed across hundreds of hospitals — was studied by researchers at University of Michigan. They found it generated so many alerts that nurses and doctors began dismissing them routinely. One analysis put the false alert rate at around 52%. When half your warnings are wrong, the warning system stops being a safety net.[/EX]

[KEY]A health AI that's right 48% of the time on its alerts isn't just unhelpful — it can actively degrade care by training clinicians to ignore warnings.[/KEY]
